column2: Use a common architecture with configuration-controlled bay counts and separate vehicle identities. Plan the late-2028 precursor as 1 vehicle with 3 probes and the 2031 mission as 2 vehicles with 7 probes each, for 14 probes total.

Use a keyed mechanical adapter and an isolated release-command interface defined in a host ICD. Start trade studies with a 28 V electrical interface, 2 independent release inhibits, and a single end-to-end host compatibility test before integration.

Initialize both designs from a 400 km circular Mars orbit and record the host state as 6 Cartesian components plus a 6 × 6 covariance. Use a 3–20 orbit targeting search as the initial planning window.

Track wet mass once at the vehicle boundary, including loaded propulsion and nitrogen. Start with an A allocation of 19 kg plus 1 kg reserve and a B allocation of 47.5 kg plus 2.5 kg reserve against the respective 20 kg and 50 kg ceilings.

Give each probe an independent sample record with its vehicle and probe IDs, acquisition time, source coordinates, estimated depth and environmental measurements. Size an initial record for 1 s time resolution and 1 mm depth encoding, with separate uncertainty fields.

Use an event-gated mission controller with measured completion before every irreversible transition. Seed the trajectory with a 125 km entry interface, 10 km extraction reference, and first probe release at 5 km, followed by 2 s spacing.

Use immutable vehicle/probe identities and per-source event journals so a reset or missing packet affects only its own status. Allocate 8 bits each to vehicle and probe identifiers and 32 bits to the per-source event sequence.

Use a dispersed six-degree-of-freedom analysis and separation verification before arming entry readiness. Begin sensitivity runs with ±5° heat-shield pointing, a 2°/s rate ceiling and at least 30 s between confirmed jettison and the model entry interface.

Use buffered 400 MHz UHF proximity transmissions under an orbiter service agreement and confirm delivery through a relay acknowledgment or ground receipt. Begin the link screen at 400 km slant range, 10 W RF output and 3 dB receiver margin.

Use a duty-cycled surface timeline with priority data return and an explicit energy reserve. Size for 24 h on A and 72 h on B, beginning with 20 Wh usable energy and reserving 4 Wh before scheduling experiment loads.

Use a configuration-specific verification matrix with a named reviewer and evidence reference for every applicable requirement. Require 100% disposition of applicable rows and 0 unapproved departures before release for flight.

Place presentation artifacts under configuration control with a filename, revision identifier, numbered slides and SHA-256 checksum. Allocate 1 manifest entry per artifact, and use the 10-slide phase map as the initial trace structure.

Use a protected side intake with a depth fiducial and independent recovered-quantity measurement. Screen the sealed assay at 2–5 cm accessible source depth and 0.25 cm³ per vessel, or the extraction branch at 1.0 ± 0.2 g of recovered soil.

Use separate, positively isolated sample and control cartridges, each leak-tested before integration. Start with 3 independently isolated fluid paths and a qualification screen of ≤1% cross-channel carryover by a nonreactive tracer.

Use an impact-supported battery with separate logic, actuator and detector power branches plus regulated RF supply. Allocate 20 Wh usable, 4 Wh for data return and an illustrative 5 A transient capacity on the main bus.

Install independent sample and detector temperature sensors, a chamber pressure sensor and a hydration proxy. Begin calibration at 1 Hz with ±0.5 °C temperature and ±0.1 kPa pressure targets, storing validity with each record.

Use a solid-state scintillator coupled to a temperature-monitored SiPM with separately recorded bias and live time. Start electronics characterization with 1 s count bins and sweep a 10–10,000 counts/s reference range for linearity and saturation.

Use a mechanically supported microcontroller and nonvolatile storage with independent commit and recovery records. Allocate 60 MB on A and 252 MB on B to the probe-science portion of the logical budget per vehicle. Screen for complete recovery of committed records after 100 power interruptions.

Use a 0.50 m independent drogue with its loads carried by structural attachments on the probe body. Start opening and impact tests at a 500 N drag screening limit and a 1,500 g₀ shock screening level, pending measured loads.

Thermally isolate the chamber and detector and monitor each with its own temperature channel. For the extraction concept, begin with a 0–5 °C sample range, a −10 to 30 °C detector housing range and a 1 W peak chamber heater allocation.

Use a body-mounted 400 MHz radiator and independent feed that remain attached after touchdown. Start with 10 W peak RF and test 3 antenna orientations over a 0–5 cm burial-depth range in representative material.

At boot, verify a signed configuration and store probe ID, firmware and calibration revisions, reset cause and a hardware-counter origin. Begin with a 64-bit monotonic count in milliseconds and a 1 s boot self-test allocation.

Gate physical actuation on chamber status, sample-sensor validity and usable energy above the return reserve. Begin with a 4 Wh reserve and invalidate environmental samples more than 2 s old. Log each blocked transition with its reason.

Use a task graph with measured energy costs and debit the reserve before authorizing another science task. Start with 60 s energy-accounting updates and a protected 4 Wh return budget in both configurations.

Use a persistent registry that assigns every sample, control and fraction its own identifier and parent record. Start with 32-bit record IDs and 1 mg quantity encoding, storing acquisition time, source channel and the reason for any rejection.

Implement explicit prepare, baseline, incubate, extract and measure states with a durable checkpoint before irreversible actuation. Budget 5 nominal states and 2 recovery outcomes, resume or inhibit, with a power-loss test at each transition.

Write raw counts together with live time, bias, detector temperature and data validity. Begin with 1 s count bins and 1 ms live-time resolution. Mark invalid intervals separately in the science record.

Apply versioned calibration and blank/recovery corrections with an uncertainty field on each derived result. Flag isotope estimates with a response-matrix condition number above 10 or when any of the 3 correction records is absent.

Use an append-only journal with a length, sequence, CRC-32 and commit marker for every record. Start with a 4 KiB write block and retain the complete raw record after reprocessing or interrupted writes.

Queue labeled science frames for retry and keep attempted transmission separate from acknowledged delivery. Begin with 256-byte payloads, 32-bit sequence numbers and a nominal 1 s transmission opportunity every 60 s.

Fuse an optical attitude reference with a three-axis gyro and invalidate estimates when sources disagree. Begin hardware tests with 100 Hz inertial data, 5 Hz optical updates and a ±2° attitude-error target.

Separate the guidance processor from independently inhibited actuator switching and monitor commands on a distinct hardware-enable path. Begin with a 100 Hz control loop and a 100 ms watchdog timeout.
Use a thrust ring that passes motor loads to the primary structure. Screen A with 100 N for 20 s, 2,000 N·s total impulse and 225 s assumed Isp; size B for a 12.8 s burn at 250 s assumed Isp.

Use a regulated nitrogen supply with pressure and temperature sensing. Start the ideal-gas sizing at 0.100 kg, 200 bar and 293 K, corresponding to about 0.435 L, with a 20 bar minimum regulation reference.
Allocate six 0.10 N jets with a 0.25 m effective lever arm and 65 s assumed Isp. Keep separately metered budgets for 0.20 m/s separation, 90° burn alignment and 180° entry alignment.
Use separate hardware arm and fire/release paths with independently reported states. Begin with 2 independent inhibits for each function and require zero unintended actions in single-fault injection.

Use a separate module battery and an isolated handover harness. Take 12 Wh usable and a 20% reserve as initial power allocations and require a 5 s powered handover window after valid status transfer begins.

Use a restrained structural ring and positively separable electrical interface to keep motor loads and heat away from the retained capsule. Start the interface trade with a 1.5 load factor, 50 mm post-release clearance and separate thermal and plume screens.

Send a structured handover record with source ID, burn status, attitude, gas and release evidence. Begin with a 10 Hz status stream and 2 independently sensed release states, each timestamped by the retained controller.

Boot from a checksum-verified A or B configuration and hold actuators inhibited until host separation and sensor checks pass. Begin with a 100 ms heartbeat check and 2 independent separation indications.

Sequence the translation jets after sensed host release and estimate clearance from relative motion. Use 0.20 m/s commanded separation and a 20 m initial clearance gate, with positive release evidence before maneuvering.

Propagate a 400 km starting orbit against the ephemeris and rank deorbit opportunities by ground-track residual. Search 3–20 orbits initially and screen against 100 km for A and 50 km for B, pending navigation and target validation.
Use a closed-loop paired-jet maneuver to acquire burn attitude. Begin with a 90° reference slew and hold pointing within ±2° and rate within 1°/s for 1 s before authorizing ignition.
Use explicit inhibited, armed, firing and completed states with measured thrust or acceleration to corroborate burn. Start time checks with 20 s for A, 12.8 s for B and a ±0.5 s diagnostic tolerance.

Use a closed-loop postburn slew with persistence before enabling release. Start the assumed bottom-mount case with a 180° turn, ±5° pointing tolerance and 2°/s rate ceiling; rederive these values when mount geometry changes.

Separate sensor, actuator, burn and release faults in the supervisor and inhibit progression when completion is unconfirmed. Start with 4 fault classes, a 100 ms invalid-sensor timeout and a 2 s release-confirmation timeout.
Debit each maneuver independently and recompute usable mass above the regulator floor. Track 3 maneuver withdrawals plus leakage against the 0.100 kg loaded reference and flag a deficit at 20 bar.

Use positive acknowledgment of a retained state record before jettison, then invalidate the removed module’s actuator handles. Begin with 2 checked transaction records and a 5 s maximum handover interval.

Use a preliminary 0.800 m sphere-cone aeroshell with a 70° half-angle from the symmetry axis. Carry a 0.200 m nose radius, 0.070 m shoulder radius and 0.746 m packaging height into the CAD and thermal trade.

Use a calibrated entry accelerometer and center/shoulder temperature sensors read by retained avionics. Begin with 100 Hz acceleration and 10 Hz temperature acquisition, each with independent quality flags.

Use a captive carrier cradle attached to the shell structure, with load-bearing mounts and independently sensed releases. Start with 4 restraints and a 1.5 preliminary ultimate-to-limit load factor for the structural trade.
Use a passively cleared cover with independent inhibits and positive open/clear sensors. Start with 2 independent clear indications and a 2 s timeout that prevents carrier extraction.

Model passive entry with an as-built mass-properties survey and Mach-dependent force/moment tables. Start with CG at 0.15D and a 0.05D static-margin screen, then test the scenario in dispersed 6-DOF runs.
Connect the extraction chute load path to the retained carrier cradle and keep it clear of the cover mechanism. Screen the 1.5 m A and 2.0 m B canopies at a 600 Pa extraction-pressure ceiling.

Trade a guarded structural bridge against forebody attachment with a restored uninterrupted TPS surface. Start CAD with a 1.5 load factor and 50 mm separation-clearance screen for each mounting option.
Run the entry data interface from retained carrier power through a separable harness. Begin with a nominal 28 V link, 5 s handover buffer and 2 source IDs identifying module and retained avionics.

Use passive separation guides to send the discard body outside the carrier path. Start the dispersion screen at ≥1 m relative clearance within 2 s, and verify lack of recontact through the first probe release.
Decode and validate the retro handover record before entering the passive-entry state. Use a CRC-32, a 2 s freshness window and 2 consistent detached indications as initial checks.
Record acceleration and temperature as separate data streams with a shared monotonic time and validity bits. Start with 100 Hz acceleration, 10 Hz thermal recording and 1 ms timestamp encoding.

Use a filtered entry phase estimator with physical altitude and pressure as independent deployment cues. Begin with a 10 km extraction reference, 600 Pa pressure ceiling and 1 s valid-state persistence.

Keep cover and extraction outputs inhibited until the measured deployment envelope and independent enables are true. Start boundary testing at a 10 km altitude reference, 600 Pa pressure ceiling and 2 separate hardware permits.
Command the cover only once after all permits are valid and wait for confirmed clearance. Use 2 agreeing switches and a 2 s confirmation timeout that holds extraction inhibited.

Arm carrier extraction after the cover-clear checks, then record measured separation in the shared journal. Begin with a 1 s minimum delay after confirmed cover clearance and a 3 s separation timeout.
Journal commands, measurements, confirmations and faults using immutable per-source sequence numbers. Budget 4 distinct record types and a 30 s ring buffer before handover.

Allocate entry and extraction functions to the retained carrier processor until discard and keep a single authority for each actuator. Use 1 active owner per function and a 5 s design handover window.

Mark discard only after sensing carrier separation, then invalidate the capsule data stream in retained avionics. Begin with 1 terminal capsule record and 0 valid capsule measurements credited after the discard event.
Use a common carrier frame with configuration-specific bay inserts and protected release paths. Allocate 3 bays and about 3 kg retained dry mass to A, and 7 bays and 8 kg retained dry mass to B.
Equip each bay with a controlled release latch and independent open and bay-clear indications. Start with 2 confirmations per bay and a 2 s release verification window.
Use reinforced risers and a qualified carrier canopy sized for each retained carrier. Start with diameters of 1.5 m for A and 2.0 m for B and a 1.5 opening-load factor for structural screening.
Fuse a descent pressure/altitude proxy with inertial and ground-range measurements where valid. Begin with a 5 km release reference, 10 Hz estimator updates and ±100 m initial altitude accuracy.

Give the carrier a dedicated controller and nonvolatile append-only event storage. Start with 4 MB of carrier event storage and verify all committed drop states survive 100 power-cycle or interrupted-write tests.
Use a separate 400 MHz carrier radio and antenna with a dedicated source ID. Size the initial status mode for a 1 s burst every 60 s at up to 10 W RF, subject to relay acceptance.
Use an independent carrier battery and buffer sized for descent, release and status transmission. Start with 15 Wh usable, a 3 Wh reserve, and a separate 4 MB event queue.

Use keyed breakaway harnesses with independent current limiting and state confirmation at each disconnect. Start with contacts that indicate separation within 100 ms and verify electrical isolation for each of the 3 or 7 probe bays.
Release probes as self-contained instrument packages with individual drogues, power and antenna structures. Use 2 s nominal spacing and a separate 0.50 m drogue for each released probe.
Restore the upstream journal only after verifying the vehicle identity, boot epoch and configuration. Check a CRC-32 on each record and test both bay layouts, 3 for A and 7 for B.
Run a quality-gated altitude and descent-state estimator. Start at 10 Hz, mark data stale after 2 s, and require valid descent through 5 km before authorizing the first release.

Schedule releases individually, retaining bay identity and requiring independent confirmation before moving to the next bay. Start with 2 s cadence and run collision sensitivity for both the 3-bay and 7-bay configurations.

Use an append-only record and a cumulative status word with independent latched states. Begin with the 9-bit A and 13-bit B reference words and verify that a retransmission preserves all previously confirmed bits.
Record command, partial release, confirmation and fault as 4 distinct evidence states. Use a CRC-32 on each journal record and test the reported state after a reset inserted at each transition.
Use independent frame sequencing with retry and duplicate suppression by carrier ID. Start with 32-bit packet sequences and 3 retry opportunities per queued priority frame.
Reserve energy and storage for high-priority fault and release records before lower-priority telemetry. Start at a 3 Wh energy floor and issue high-buffer alerts at 80% occupancy.
Use predicted contact and queue priority to decide when to retry or buffer status. Begin with 60 s checks and an illustrative 30 min blackout test with no premature delivery confirmation.

On sensed terminal contact, inhibit unreleased bays and transmit terminal status until timeout or reserve cutoff. Start with 3 consecutive contact samples, a 15 min status window and a 3 Wh reserve floor.

Track a single ledger with separate columns for wet mass, retro propellant used, each nitrogen withdrawal, discarded hardware and retained entry mass. Audit every event boundary to 0.01 kg and verify initial closure against 20 kg for A and 50 kg for B.

Replace the A propulsion allocation with 0.906414 kg motor propellant, 0.100 kg nitrogen and 1.500 kg dry module. Scale the remaining components by the available mass divided by the 17.5 kg reference nonpropulsion allocation, yielding about 1.999267 kg per probe and 2.998900 kg retained carrier dry mass at 20 kg.

Use a traceable free-space link budget and repeat it with measured antenna and relay data. Seed it with 400 MHz, 400 km, 10 W RF, 0 dBi transmit gain, 6 dBi receive gain, 6 dB losses and a −120 dBm receive threshold. Screen candidates for 3 dB margin.

Track usable energy, peak current and return reserves separately for each vehicle. Seed the probe calculation with 20 Wh usable, a 0.2 W average-load reference and a 1 s transmission burst per 60 s. With 4 Wh reserved, the remaining average allowances are about 0.67 W over 24 h and 0.22 W over 72 h.

Split the 64 MB A and 256 MB B reference data budgets per vehicle between the carrier packet/event queue and the released probes. Start with 4 MB for carrier events and packets and 60 MB for A or 252 MB for B probe science in aggregate, with 20% headroom inside each allocation. Validate overhead and write rate before rounding to installed capacities.

Use a two-location thermal model with explicit thickness, material and soak assumptions, then correlate it against material tests. Compare the 15 mm live reference with a 60 mm trade candidate under 1.5× heating and 300 s soak.

Correlate penetration and shock predictions with instrumented material tests and measured accessible sample recovery. Start with 3 representative media, a 50–100 m/s impact-speed sweep and a separate 2–5 cm accessible-depth target.

Assign processor, power source, data ownership and actuator authority for each interface and handover. Require 1 named owner per function and exercise 2 handovers, retro to retained avionics and capsule functions to independent carrier operations.

Sign the configuration manifest with build and calibration identifiers and store it with every mission data export. Use SHA-256 for file identity, 2 software slots for recovery and a 32-bit configuration ID in the telemetry schema.

Use a six-state evidence field that distinguishes commanded, measured, estimated, inferred, unknown and failed. Keep relay receipt separate and inject at least 1 fault per state, with 0 confirmation bits set by command issuance alone.
Use a per-source monotonic counter and a boot epoch, with time-sync uncertainty stored separately. Begin with millisecond ticks, a 60 s resync interval and a 10 ms two-clock ordering-error screen.

Wrap raw measurements in a versioned schema with source identity, unit, time, calibration ID and quality flags. Start with CRC-32 framing and exercise 3 explicit quality states: valid, missing and invalid.

Test nominal, boundary, reset and fault paths in software and on representative electronics. Plan 100% coverage of safety-relevant transitions and at least 1 hardware test for every independent inhibit.

Version models, settings and inputs and export a reproducible physical event timeline. Record a SHA-256 source fingerprint, store time in seconds and compare selected numeric outputs against a 1% reproducibility tolerance.

Use a fault tree and an exercised response for every critical actuator and handover. Start with a 100 ms invalid-data timeout and a 2 s release timeout, checking for 0 false completion records across the fault campaign.

Carry the sealed assay and incubation/extraction assay as 2 separate configuration-controlled candidates until review. Use the existing 0.25 cm³ per vessel and approximately 1 g soil references to size their separate sample paths.

Design a blinded control panel for time-zero, reagent-only, matched matrix, inactivated reference and recovery controls. Start with 5 control classes and 3 replicate pairs per condition for preflight characterization.

Measure and log chamber temperature, pressure and hydration history with each science record. Screen distinct environmental envelopes of −10 to 0 °C for the sealed concept and 0–5 °C for the extraction concept, beginning with 1 Hz logging.

Use a measurement ledger separating input activity, recovered gas, liquid and solid activity, and estimated losses. Start with 4 accounting categories after dosing and an illustrative 80–120% closure band to flag unexplained losses during ground controls.

Use a calibrated two-channel response model with uncertainty propagation and explicit cross-talk controls. Start with a 2 × 2 response matrix, 3 reference mixtures and a condition-number screening limit of 10.

Predeclare decision thresholds and use independently characterized blanks and positive references to validate sensitivity. Begin with 20 blank runs, 3 replicate pairs per condition and an illustrative 5% false-positive ceiling.

Build separate battery and activity timelines for both science concepts, including detector, valves, heaters and relay reserve. Start with 24 h on A, 72 h on B and 4 Wh reserved for return. Treat the 1–5-sol sealed concept as an unresolved schedule trade.

Transmit the raw measurement and qualified analysis together with uncertainty and context fields. Start with 3 interpretation flags: below decision threshold, above threshold pending review, and invalid.

Use separate sealed sample and control paths with preflight cleanliness and compatibility verification. Begin with 3 isolated flow paths and an illustrative ≤1% carryover limit using an inert witness tracer.

Compare candidate optical channels against known reference materials and matrix interferents before drawing a selectivity conclusion. Start with 3 target-species reference classes, 3 replicate pairs per class and a 5% false-positive screening target.
